text: What is the decisive advantage of a phase-change-material (PCM) synapse over a thermally tuned microring for holding a weight?
choices: The PCM weight can be updated faster during inference
The PCM cell amplifies the optical signal as it stores the weight
The PCM cell is volatile, so it refreshes its weight automatically
Non-volatility: it holds its state for years at zero static power, whereas a thermally tuned ring dissipates about 1 mW continuously
explanation: The book emphasizes non-volatility: the PCM phase persists for years at zero static power, paying its energy cost once at write time (~nJ), whereas a thermally tuned ring pays about 1 mW forever. Choice 2 inverts the key property (PCM is non-volatile), a passive PCM cell attenuates rather than amplifies (choice 1), and update speed is not the cited advantage (choice 0).
